eventMetadata.context_description:
**Strong El Niño development combined with the long-term anthropogenic warming trend has driven August 2026 global mean surface temperatures well above 1.29 °C above the 1850–1900 baseline, producing the market’s near-certain (>99 %) consensus for that outcome.** Observational data through late August show the month tracking toward roughly 1.6 °C (with ranges centered near 1.56–1.68 °C), fueled by record extra-polar sea-surface temperatures peaking at 21.1 °C and Niño-3.4 indices already exceeding +2.7 °C. These conditions exceed recent high-anomaly months such as July 2023 and 2024 while aligning with Berkeley Earth, Copernicus, and ERA5 analyses that place 2026 on a trajectory for multiple monthly records. The dominant driver remains the superposition of greenhouse-gas forcing and a rapidly intensifying El Niño whose subsurface heat reservoir continues to surface. 

Realistic challenges to the >1.29 °C threshold would require substantial downward revisions in final blended datasets or an abrupt weakening of the El Niño not currently indicated by multi-model ensembles; both remain low-probability given the month’s near-completion and consistent observational signals.
